observations: Says non-motorized boating is legal on the Albuquerque Rio Grande.
Identifies limited boating access on the north side of the Central Avenue Bridge on both river banks and notes that boaters walk from parking to the river.
sources.name: City of Albuquerque — Enjoying the Rio Grande
sources.limits: Confirms public boating access in the Central Avenue area but does not give a surveyed landing coordinate or describe the precise carry path.

observations: Identifies the bosque parking lot at the southwest corner of Central Avenue and the river.
Describes work on the parking lot/access road and plans to rebuild and improve the river access point for paddle sports.
sources.name: City of Albuquerque — Westside Bosque Improvements Underway (March 28, 2025)
sources.limits: The announcement does not publish the landing toe coordinate or confirm the present construction/maintenance state of the ramp.

observations: Publishes 35.08728077195977,-106.68221819147834 as the Central Avenue Access GPS point after directions to the Sunset SW parking area.
Says the parking area is managed by MRGCD and Albuquerque Open Space and describes the route from Sunset Road to the parking area.
sources.name: Quiet Waters — Middle Rio Grande public access information
sources.limits: The coordinate is a parking/access-area pin, not a surveyed river-edge entry point.

observations: The City GIS Open Space layer returns Rio Grande Valley State Park, with status Open To Public, for a polygon intersecting the access coordinate.
sources.name: City of Albuquerque AGIS — Open Space feature layer
sources.limits: Confirms the public open-space parcel, not boat launch permission or the water-entry toe; the City boating guidance supplies the boating-access evidence.

observations: Fresh candidate-centered NHD checks return complete hydrography coverage and no source issues for either affected public route.

The Central Avenue access-area control classifies both exact-coordinate occurrences as review; the separate Rio Bravo take-out on rio-grande-central-rio-bravo remains suspicious at 442 feet from its matched flowline.
sources.name: USGS National Hydrography Dataset — targeted route audit
sources.limits: Hydrography offsets show distance to generalized mapped flowlines/water polygons, not the surveyed location or current condition of an access ramp.

decision: Retain the exact public parking/access-area coordinate; do not use it as a claim of exact water entry. Continue to show review status and instruct users to carry to and inspect the current landing.
